date_note: Insurance Business says the case was removed to federal court on 20 November 2026; the complaint was filed on 26 October 2026.
exec: A cyber-insurance dispute shows how a policy's definitions can change the limit paid after a supplier's ransomware attack.
geo_basis: plaintiff's home area stated as Miami-Dade and Broward counties; Miami used
plain: A Miami Jaguar Land Rover dealer says its cyber insurer, At-Bay, applied a lower limit to its losses from the Jaguar Land Rover ransomware attack. The claims are untested.
summary: Insurance Business reports that Warren Henry Automobiles, a Miami luxury dealership group, sued its cyber insurer At-Bay over a claim tied to the Jaguar Land Rover ransomware attack. The complaint alleges At-Bay classified the JLR platforms under a $1 million tier instead of the $5 million limit, a $4 million difference. The article says the allegations are untested and gives no At-Bay statement.
title: Luxury dealer sues At-Bay over $4M ransomware coverage gap, Insurance Business reports

validation.note: Insurance Business only; the complaint and court filings were not read and At-Bay's own statement was not found.

evidence.quote: The full $5 million contingent business interruption limit versus $1 million - a $4 million difference
